q: Your Notes app hides other people's notes in the screens. Why is that not enough?
o: Screens run slowly on old phones
Anyone can send requests straight to Firestore with your public config
Firestore deletes hidden notes
Google reviews your screens before launch
why: The client talks to the database directly. Only security rules decide which requests succeed.

q: In an update rule, which check stops a user from changing a note's owner?
o: request.auth != null
resource.data.text is string
request.resource.data.ownerId == resource.data.ownerId
request.time > resource.data.createdAt
why: It compares the owner after the write with the stored owner, so the owner field cannot change.

q: With owner-only read rules, getDocs(collection(db, "notes")) fails. What should you do?
o: Add where("ownerId", "==", uid) to the query
Allow read for all signed-in users
Use the Admin SDK in the browser
Wait a few minutes and retry
why: Rules are not filters. The query must only be able to return documents the caller may read.

q: A rule on users/{uid} also protects users/{uid}/tokens.
why: Rules do not cascade to subcollections. The tokens subcollection needs its own match and allow.

q: Your database still uses the test mode rule. What is the real risk?
o: Only the app gets slower
Anyone can read, change or delete all data until the date
Only signed-in users can write
Writes are free until the date
why: The test mode rule matches every document and allows all reads and writes until the date in it.

q: A Cloud Function updates another user's note and it works, even with strict rules. Why?
o: The rules file failed to deploy
Functions run in test mode
The Admin SDK bypasses security rules
The emulator is still running
why: Server code with the Admin SDK ignores rules, so it must make its own checks.

q: A get() lookup inside a rule is free if the request is denied.
why: Each get() or exists() is billed as a read, even when the request is denied.

q: Which test best proves your owner-only read rule works?
o: Ana reads her own note and it succeeds
Ben reads Ana's note and assertFails passes
The app starts with no errors
The console shows no warnings
why: A rule that allows too much shows no errors in normal use. Only a test of the denied case catches the leak.
